findings.finding: Holam confirmed in the tight detail (s8-header-rosh-detail.png). It is a distinct round dot above the top left of ר, in the gap between ר and א where a holam on ר is usually placed. It is clearly apart from both letters.

The right-hand shin dot is still not confirmed independently. In the tight detail, the right head of ש looks like a thickened, rounded blob that rises a little above the other two heads. That fits a shin dot fused into the head stroke, but I can't see a separate dot with white space between it and the head. I am not reporting this as a difference, and there is no sign of a left (sin) dot. I can't tell from this image alone whether the dot is printed or whether I would just be assuming the standard spelling. The candidate's שׁ is unchanged, but this one mark needs a human ruling or a sharper scan before I can approve it.

The shin dot is confirmed on the right side: a distinct dot above the right head of ש, separated from the letter and not over its left head. The dagesh is confirmed: a dark dot in the middle of the ש, between the arms and above the base. The other pointing confirmed again at this enlargement: patach under ה, qamatz under ש, qamatz under נ.

The small mark on the top left of the final ה is still there in the tight detail. It sits on the top stroke, not inside the letter, so it is not a mappiq. It is not a rafe bar or an accent either. It stays a printing blemish with no glyph value. This agrees with the first report.

Both shin dots are confirmed on the right side (s8-header-sheni-shel-detail.png). Each ש has a distinct dot above its right head, with no left dot. Vowels confirmed again at this enlargement: tsere under ש of שֵׁנִי, hiriq under נ, segol under ש of שֶׁל. The ל of the preceding לֵיל can also be seen at the right edge of the crop.

Carried from the first report and not seen again in the new details: there is no meteg under מ, and the dot under the patach is an ink speck. In the first report: patach on מ, hataf patach on ע, hiriq on ר. The tsere in לֵיל was also read in the first report.
Citation carried from the first report and not seen again: דברים י״א י״ג, with gershayim printed in both numbers and no end punctuation.
Citation carried from the first report and not seen again: במדבר ט״ו ל״ז, with gershayim printed in both numbers and no end punctuation.

exact_heading: מַעֲרִיב לֵיל שֵׁנִי שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
exact_heading_notes: The text matches the candidate. Every mark is now confirmed from the source except the right-hand shin dot on ש of רֹאשׁ, which looks fused into the head stroke and can't be confirmed as a separate dot. No meteg on מ. The mark over the final ה is a blemish.
scope_limitations: This covers only the source paratext reading: the s8 heading and the two corrected citations. It does not cover prayer blocks, JLPTEI encoding, alignment or order, export, or page numbers. I read the three new tight detail images directly. I did not check their SHA-256 hashes against header_detail_images.json. The marks on מַעֲרִיב and לֵיל, and the citation gershayim, come from the first report's crops, with the scope stated there. I did not look at them again here. As before, the printed gershayim can't be told apart from two gereshes (׳׳), and I write them as U+05F4. No new human ruling was supplied. The only open item is the shin dot on רֹאשׁ, and status is changes_required only because of it. If that dot is confirmed, this review can be approved with no change to the text.
